subject: LLM access transport proposal for regulated sites
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LLM access transport proposal for regulated sites

Alex — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our conversation, Starlite needs a recommended transport approach for connecting your on-prem and VPC workloads to a Redwood Private deployment while preserving compliance and predictable latency.

I put together three pragmatic options (high-level) and attached a short mutual action plan and a network diagram for discussion:

- VPC peering (cross-account peering): low-latency, no additional egress-interface endpoints, but requires overlapping-subnet remediation and does not support cross-region peering in the same way.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): strong security posture (no cross-account route table changes required), fine-grained endpoint policy, but per-hour ENI + data processing charges and requires NAT/egress considerations for on-prem traffic.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPSec managed tunnel): lowest initial ops friction for on-prem, predictable egress billing and termination control, but higher and variable latency and lower throughput without dedicated appliances.

Can you confirm the following so we can tailor the recommendation?
1) Do you have overlapping CIDR ranges between the Starlite VPCs we would talk to and the Redwood VPCs (or are you open to renumbering)?
2) Which regions are in scope for the pilot (we showed us-west-2 today)?
3) Do you have appliance bandwidth guarantees for IPSec (e.g., SD-WAN/NGFW with BGP)?

Next step: once you confirm the three bullets above, Ben + Kim and I will draft a preferred-path recommendation and an ops checklist (firewalls, NAT, monitoring hooks).

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hannah — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers below and a few follow-ups from infra: 

1) CIDR: we currently have two VPCs with 10.0.0.0/16 and 10.1.0.0/16; we do not want to renumber during pilot.
2) Pilot region: us-west-2 only.
3) IPsec appliance: we have an F5/NGFW pair with an advertised 1Gbps capability; our WAN provider supports GRE+IPSec.

Infra asks:
- If we use peering, will we be able to keep our existing subnet ranges without NAT?
- For PrivateLink, can your side handle asymmetric flows (we egress some traffic through a proxy chain)?
- Any guidance on monitoring—what telemetry do you require for audits?

I'll attach an internal answers workbook (starlite-networking-answers.xlsx) with the topology details.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LLM access transport proposal for regulated sites

Team — drafting a recommended path for the pilot given Alex's constraints (no renumbering, us-west-2, F5 appliances). My thoughts: 

- Peering: ruled out for the pilot. Cross-account peering would require Starlite to create routes for Redwood subnets into their routing fabric; with the 10.x overlap risk we can't recommend renumbering during the pilot. Peering also requires us-to-customer route acceptance, which sometimes causes ops delays.

- PrivateLink (recommended primary):
  * Pros: No route table changes in customer's VPCs, interface endpoints provide per-service access control, and traffic does not rely on customer-wide routing. This maps well for regulated workloads where customers want minimal lateral exposure.
  * Cons: Endpoint cost (ENI + data processed). On-prem traffic will need to egress to the endpoint — we should validate proxy/NAT behavior with their appliance. We can provide guidance for health checks and endpoint scaling.

- Site-to-site VPN (recommended fallback/bridge):
  * Pros: Quick to stand up, full control of termination, supports on-prem-only traffic without re-architecting. Good when customers insist on appliance termination.
  * Cons: Latency variability and throughput limits if they have a 1Gbps appliance; also increases operational burden for L2/L3 troubleshooting.

Telemetry and audit: we should ask for BGP peering metadata (if used), SNAT mapping expectations, and sampling of flow logs. For our SOC/Security book, we need: VPC flow logs (7 days for pilot), VPN tunnel event logs, and a signed network diagram.

Action items I propose:
1) Primary: PrivateLink endpoint + strict endpoint policy in us-west-2 for pilot workloads.
2) Bridge: IPSec VPN from their F5 to a dedicated Redwood VPN concentrator as a failover for on-prem-only calls or heavy data bursts.
3) Deliverable: updated mutual action plan (Hannah) with steps, firewall rules, and test vectors (ping, curl to health endpoints, simulated 200 RPS).

Kimberly, can you confirm if Redwood can offer a per-endpoint throughput SLA or suggested sizing guidance? I will capture billing expectations for the customer.

-ben

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@starlitehealth.com>, infra-ops@starlitehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LLM access transport proposal for regulated sites — next steps and MWP

Alex — thanks for the quick turn. Team synced and attached a revised mutual action plan (redwood-mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf) and a proposed diagram (proposed-diagram-v2.png) that follows Ben's recommendation: primary path = PrivateLink in us-west-2; failover = managed IPSec to our VPN concentrator.

Quick answers to infra questions:
- Peering + existing CIDR: peering without renumbering will cause route conflicts (10/8 overlaps are common). We can't safely recommend peering during the pilot.
- PrivateLink and asymmetric flows: Redwood's endpoint accepts connections initiated from the customer into the endpoint ENIs. As long as the proxy chain preserves source IP or the proxy performs consistent SNAT behavior, flows will be stable. We'll document expected headers and health-check endpoints.
- Telemetry: for audit purposes we require VPC flow logs (retention min 7 days), a packet-loss and latency baseline during the pilot window, and VPN tunnel state logs if you use the IPSec fallback. We'll provide a short checklist for logs to ship to our security team.

Next steps / timeline:
- This week: Starlite confirms no-blocking firewall rules and shares the NAT/proxy behavior (infra to fill the workbook).
- Next week: we'll provision a PrivateLink endpoint in our test account, share an endpoint DNS name and policy, and run a connectivity smoke test.
- Pilot: 2 weeks run with test vectors, telemetry collection, and a post-pilot SLO review.

If this aligns, please mark the workbook as "confirmed" and we'll schedule a 30-min runbook session with Connor for the VPN fallback configuration.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
